claims.field: name, description, starting price, end time, image reference
claims.statement: Mohammed's creation operation writes five user-supplied fields — product name, description, starting price, end time, image reference — exactly once; all five are immutable for the auction's lifetime, with no edit screen, control, or route permitted. All five are required; there are no optional fields and no reserve-price field.
claims.source: ARCHITECTURE.md:509 (§9.3 auction field table); PRD.md:474 (FR-CREATE-01), PRD.md:479 (FR-CREATE-03), PRD.md:510 (FR-CREATE-24); GITHUB_PLAN.md:369 (AUC-01)

claims.statement: Owner is system-assigned at creation from the server-side verified session, never from the request payload; a crafted request naming a different owner is attributed to the authenticated caller. Ownership is permanent and non-transferable.
claims.source: PRD.md:475 (FR-CREATE-02), PRD.md:508 (FR-CREATE-22); ARCHITECTURE.md:510 (§9.3 'System-assigned at creation'); GITHUB_PLAN.md:375 (AUC-07)

claims.statement: Status is system-assigned Active immediately at creation; there is no persisted Draft state (Draft exists only as the pre-submission form state) and no scheduled future start. The auction is publicly visible in the listing at once and the creator is redirected to its detail page.
claims.source: PRD.md:516-519 (FR-CREATE-26..29), PRD.md:753 (BR-14), PRD.md:1205 ('On Draft'), PRD.md:1226 (LC-02); ARCHITECTURE.md:118; GITHUB_PLAN.md:376 (AUC-08)

claims.statement: At creation the auction's current price equals its starting price with an empty bid history. This post-condition is assigned to Mohammed's workstream: M-09 'Publication behavior — auction becomes Active immediately, current price = starting price, empty history' sits in Mohammed's work breakdown (traces FR-CREATE-26→29, BR-14), and AUC-08 (Mohammed's epic) repeats it. Lifecycle transition T1 confirms: 'Auction created; owner set from session; current price = starting price; history empty'.
claims.source: TEAM.md:595 (M-09, in §13.2 Mohammed's breakdown); PRD.md:518 (FR-CREATE-28), PRD.md:1057, PRD.md:1213 (T1); GITHUB_PLAN.md:376 (AUC-08)

claims.statement: Doc tension on who may write the initial value: ARCHITECTURE §9.3 categorizes current price as 'Derived — never user-writable ... Only the bid operation (BR-07, BR-13)' with no carve-out for creation-time initialization, while FR-CREATE-28/M-09/T1 require the creation path (Mohammed's) to set it to the starting price. S0-11's clause 'Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else' constrains Rayan only and does not name the creation-time writer. The contract should state the carve-out explicitly: creation initializes it once; thereafter only the bid operation writes it.

Validation on the value Mohammed writes: required, numeric, strictly greater than zero, in SAR, at most two decimal places; no maximum exists and none may be introduced — a large value must never be rejected for size. Enforced server-side; bypassing the form is rejected identically.

Validation on the value Mohammed writes: a future timestamp between 5 minutes and 7 days ahead, inclusive at both ends, measured against server time never client time; stored and compared in UTC, displayed in the viewer's local timezone. After creation it is immutable and no user may change it.

Each listing entry shows thumbnail, name, current price, status, and time remaining. FR-LIST-03 defines the value AND its label: 'Current price must be the starting price when there are no bids, and the highest valid bid otherwise. It must be labelled unambiguously (e.g. `Current bid: 250 SAR` vs `Starting price: 100 SAR`)'. The listing is not subscribed to realtime — prices are current as of load (live listing prices are Should Have, FR-LIST-10).

The detail page shows current price in SAR as the most visually prominent element, and must clearly distinguish 'Starting price: 100 SAR (no bids yet)' from 'Current bid: 250 SAR'. When there are no bids it must ALSO make clear a first bid of exactly the starting price is acceptable. AUC-14 assigns the region to Mohammed with 'Rayan supplies the value and its updates — Mohammed never computes the price'. Separately, Rayan's bid history region shows 'No bids yet' when empty.
claims.source: PRD.md:544-545 (FR-DETAIL-05, FR-DETAIL-06), PRD.md:551 (FR-DETAIL-12), PRD.md:1571 (NFR-USA-04); GITHUB_PLAN.md:382 (AUC-14); TEAM.md:603 (M-17)

claims.statement: The label discriminator CANNOT be 'current price == starting price'. BR-29/SC-55 accept a first bid exactly equal to the starting price, after which current price still equals starting price yet the UI must have switched: EC-23 states 'before any bid it says bidding starts at 100 SAR; after the first bid it requires more than 100 SAR', and SC-56 rejects a second equal bid. Therefore the only correct discriminator for both FR-LIST-03 and FR-DETAIL-06 is whether at least one accepted bid exists — bid existence, not price comparison.
claims.source: PRD.md:768 (BR-29), PRD.md:1623-1624 (SC-55, SC-56), PRD.md:1414 (EC-23), PRD.md:545 (FR-DETAIL-06), PRD.md:525 (FR-LIST-03)

claims.statement: Bid existence appears in NO version of the frozen field list. GITHUB_PLAN S0-11 freezes six read fields (id, owner, status, end time, starting price, current price); TEAM.md §10.3 and §9.3 list a different six (id, owner, status, end time, starting price, 'whether the auction exists' — current price absent, contradicting TEAM.md:369 which says BR-03 needs current price); ARCHITECTURE §19.3 lists five (owner, status, end time, starting price, current price). None includes a bid count or has-bids indicator, yet both the display label (FR-DETAIL-06) and the server-side BR-28 branch require it.
claims.source: GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 (S0-11 AC); TEAM.md:421-422 (§10.3), TEAM.md:369, TEAM.md:372 (§9.3); ARCHITECTURE.md:1295 (§19.3)

claims.statement: The bid operation itself needs bid existence to pick the BR-28 branch: ARCHITECTURE §13.2 step 3 re-reads 'owner, status, end time, current price, bid count' inside the lock, and step 7 branches 'no bids yet → amount >= starting price; has bids → amount > current price'. §13.2a closes: 'The whole amount rule is BR-28, and it has exactly two branches... Anything else is not a rule of this product.' 'bid count' appears exactly once across all four documents as operation state (plus 'empty history' at creation) — it is never defined as an auction record field in §9.3's field table.
claims.source: ARCHITECTURE.md:817, ARCHITECTURE.md:829-831, ARCHITECTURE.md:871 (§13.2, §13.2a); ARCHITECTURE.md:507-512 (§9.3, no bid-count row)

claims.statement: The discriminator lives on RAYAN'S side of the boundary. ARCHITECTURE §9.4: 'Mohammed's pages read the field. Rayan's operation writes it. Neither computes it independently.' TEAM.md §11: 'Rayan supplies the value and its updates' for the current-price region; TEAM.md:267 for the listing: 'Mohammed builds the listing; Rayan supplies how the price is obtained.' The Bid entity and its history are Rayan's (ARCHITECTURE §9.1), so bid existence is derivable only from Rayan's data or from state Rayan's operation writes. Since deriving the label from price equality would be Mohammed computing (and computing wrongly, per BR-29), the labeled state — not just the number — must arrive from Rayan.
claims.source: ARCHITECTURE.md:529-538 (§9.4), ARCHITECTURE.md:489 (§9.1), ARCHITECTURE.md:989 (§14.6); TEAM.md:500 (§11), TEAM.md:267; GITHUB_PLAN.md:382 (AUC-14), GITHUB_PLAN.md:575

claims.statement: On the detail page, price updates arrive only through Rayan's per-auction realtime subscription; Mohammed's page provides the live region and passes the auction id, and 'must not add a second, competing update mechanism'. §14.3 requires current price, new history entries, status→Ended, and outcome to be delivered live; the minimum acceptable bid is 'recomputed client-side from the new price'. On disconnect/reconnect the page resynchronizes by re-reading price, history, and status — realtime is never a substitute for the authoritative read.

The same inclusive/exclusive discriminator drives Rayan's own surface: BID-06 requires the minimum shown before submission with the distinction 'unmistakable' — 'Bidding starts at 100 SAR' with no bids, 'Enter more than 250 SAR' once bidding has begun. Rejection messages differ the same way: 'Bidding starts at X SAR' (below starting, no bids) vs 'Your bid must be higher than X SAR' (has bids). Note AUC-14 (Mohammed's region) ALSO must 'make clear a first bid of exactly the starting price is acceptable' — the two owned surfaces express the same fact and must agree.

One SAR representation for storing, comparing, and formatting, agreed in S0-12 (Rayan primary, Mohammed required reviewer): exact decimal, two places, never floating point, no maximum, one display format across listing, detail, bid input, history, and results — the same amount never formatted two ways. Mohammed owns creation input and price display; Rayan owns current-price correctness. Neither may proceed with a different representation.
claims.source: TEAM.md:464-487 (§11 money rule); GITHUB_PLAN.md:264 (S0-12); PRD.md:493 (FR-CREATE-13), PRD.md:1546-1547 (NFR-DAT-05, NFR-DAT-08)

claims.statement: A third display state exists after close with zero bids: FR-END-09 — no final price is recorded and 'the starting price is retained for display only'. EC-05: the ended view says 'Auction ended — no bids, no winner', history still shows 'No bids yet', and this is a normal outcome, never an error. So the starting price outlives the Active phase as a display value on Mohammed's ended views even though the four close-write fields (status, final price, winner, close time) are Rayan's.
claims.source: PRD.md:690 (FR-END-09), PRD.md:1392 (EC-05); GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 (S0-11 four close fields), GITHUB_PLAN.md:385 (AUC-17); TEAM.md:443 (§10.5)

claims.statement: The physical seam is fixed by S0-13: Mohammed's files are page shell + data loading, product content, status label + countdown, and the current-price display region; Rayan's files are bid input + feedback, bid history list, and outcome banner. The page mounts Rayan's components and passes the auction id; neither developer edits the other's files. So whatever mechanism carries the has-bids discriminator, it must cross a file boundary — it cannot be an ad-hoc computation inside Mohammed's region.

openQuestions: Which six-field list is canonical for S0-11? GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 includes current price; TEAM.md:421 (§10.3) and TEAM.md:372 (§9.3) replace it with 'whether the auction exists' while TEAM.md:369 in the same section says BR-03 needs current price; ARCHITECTURE.md:1295 lists five fields with no id and no existence entry. The contract must name one authoritative list.

How does the display side learn 'no bids yet'? No document defines a mechanism, and price equality is provably wrong (BR-29/SC-55/EC-23). Undecided options the contract must pick from: (a) a bid-count or has-bids field on the auction record, written by Rayan's bid operation alongside current price; (b) Mohammed's read path checking emptiness of Rayan's bid history; (c) Rayan supplying a composite price value that carries its own label state. Each has different ownership and write-permission consequences.

Is the 'bid count' that ARCHITECTURE.md:817 re-reads inside the lock a stored auction-record field or derived in-transaction from Rayan's bid table? If stored, it is a seventh shared field missing from S0-11's frozen list, someone must initialize it at creation (M-09 says 'empty history' but names no counter), and Rayan writing it contradicts the S0-11 clause 'Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else' (GITHUB_PLAN.md:263) unless the clause is amended.

Who performs the creation-time write of current price = starting price? FR-CREATE-28/M-09 make it a post-condition of Mohammed's creation path, but ARCHITECTURE.md:511 (§9.3) says current price is writable 'Only [by] the bid operation' with no creation carve-out. The contract should record the carve-out explicitly so neither Claude session 'fixes' the other's write.

What concrete shape does 'Rayan supplies how the price is obtained' take for the listing (TEAM.md:267)? The listing is not realtime-subscribed (ARCHITECTURE.md:947) and reads up to 100 rows in one query for NFR-PERF-01, so it presumably reads the current-price field plus the same has-bids discriminator per row — but no document defines whether that is a shared query, a view, or a helper Rayan owns.

Does the ended-with-no-bids state need a third price label distinct from FR-DETAIL-06's two active-state labels? FR-END-09 keeps the starting price 'for display only' and EC-05 mandates 'no bids, no winner' wording, but no document specifies how the price region labels the retained starting price on an ended auction.

Both AUC-14 (Mohammed's price region, GITHUB_PLAN.md:382) and BID-06 (Rayan's minimum display, GITHUB_PLAN.md:449) are required to communicate that a first bid may equal the starting price. The documents do not say which surface carries the canonical wording or how the two avoid drifting — worth one line in the contract given three separate Claude sessions will each invent copy.

claims.statement: The finalization operation begins by locking the auction row (step 1: 'Lock the auction row'), and realtime subscriptions are scoped per auction, not globally — a viewer receives only the auction they are watching. The auction id is therefore both the lock target for all three closing triggers and the channel key for the realtime projection.

The stored status is the idempotency guard for closing: finalization step 2 is 'If already Ended → return unchanged', explicitly tied to BR-17 and SC-32, and 'because the operation is idempotent, all three triggers can fire for the same auction with no ill effect'. The sweep's selection ('auctions past their end time and not yet finalized') also reads status as the finalized/not-finalized marker. Re-running close processing must change nothing (EC-19, SC-32).

Status has exactly two persisted values: Active and Ended. Draft is 'conceptual only — not persisted', Cancelled 'does not exist' (BR-30), and Ended is terminal with no transition out (BR-15, FR-END-18). PRD §12.4 explicitly forbids building a Cancelled state, any transition out of Ended, or any manual closing control.

The stored status flag is never an input to bid eligibility — 'bidding eligibility is determined by server time against the end time, not by the stored status flag' (LC-03), and ARCHITECTURE §15.2 states this is 'what allows a scheduled sweep rather than a per-auction timer': a delay in flipping the flag cannot corrupt the outcome. The flag's only load-bearing read is the finalization idempotency check and the sweep's not-yet-finalized predicate; everything else derives ended-ness from the clock (EC-04 shows an expired-but-unprocessed auction as Ended).

All three closing triggers read end time: T1 (scheduled sweep) 'finds auctions past their end time and not yet finalized'; T2 fires when 'a viewer opens an auction whose time has passed'; T3 fires when 'a bid arrives after the end time' — the bid operation's own step 4 compares end time against the database clock. Finalization itself re-reads it inside the lock (step 3: 'If end time not yet passed → do nothing'). Because the end time is fixed at creation with no anti-sniping (BR-36), 'which auctions have expired is a stable question'.

claims.field: status, final price, winner, close time
claims.statement: Finalization writes exactly four fields, transactionally, in one commit: 'Record: status Ended, final price, winner (or explicitly none), close time' (step 5), then 'Commit → Realtime broadcasts the change' (step 6). This matches FR-END-08 ('at close the system must permanently record: ended status, actual close time, final price, and winner identity (or explicitly none)') and TEAM.md R-21. Once recorded, the outcome is immutable (SEC-I2, LC-06).

Both outcome fields must be representable as explicitly absent: zero bids ends 'with no winner and no final price' as 'a normal path, not an error' that 'must not block or delay finalization' (EC-05, ARCHITECTURE §15.7). FR-END-09: with no bids there is no final price and 'the starting price is retained for display only'. There are exactly two outcomes — a winner, or no bids — never a third, because no reserve exists (BR-35).

Closing does NOT read the auction record's current price: winner determination is 'read from the recorded bid history inside the finalization transaction' (step 4: 'Determine highest valid bid, BR-06'), and the recorded winner must always equal the highest bid in history, independently recomputable (SC-29, NFR-DAT-04). The closing mechanism's reads from the auction record itself are only: id (lock), status (idempotency guard), end time (expiry check) — plus the bid history table.
claims.source: ARCHITECTURE.md:1028-1031 (§15.3 steps 1-4), 1094, 1100 (§15.7); TEAM.md:369 ('Closing needs the end time too')

claims.statement: The realtime projection, by contrast, requires current price to live ON the auction record: ARCHITECTURE §14.3 lists 'Current price — Must — Auction record change' as a delivery source, and §9.4 fixes that it 'lives on the auction record ... written only by the bid operation, in the same transaction as the bid it derives from'. For Rayan's realtime half, this settles the TEAM.md 10.3 six-field discrepancy (TEAM.md:421 omits current price) in favor of the GITHUB_PLAN S0-11 list that includes it — the projection cannot broadcast a price change from a field that does not exist on the record.

The realtime payload content, per the ARCHITECTURE §14.3 must-deliver table and PRD §13.1: from the auction record change — current price, status → Ended, and outcome (winner, final price) 'in the same change'; from the bid insert — the new history entry (amount, display name, timestamp per PRD 13.1 and RT-S1). Two things are explicitly NOT pushed: minimum acceptable bid ('recomputed client-side from the new price') and time remaining ('ticks locally from the server-supplied end time — no push needed', FR-RT-02).

End time must be present in the initial auction read (not the realtime push): the countdown 'counts down continuously in the client' from 'the authoritative end time [that] comes from the server' (FR-RT-02), updating at least once per second (NFR-RT-03). So the realtime contract's dependency on end time is a read-at-load dependency on the auction record, not a payload field.

Email addresses cannot appear in any realtime payload, and this must be structural, not filtered: emails live in Supabase Auth, 'the publicly-readable table simply does not contain an email address, so no policy mistake, join, or realtime payload can leak one' (§9.2); RLS applies to realtime subscriptions identically (§11.1, SEC-Z9, RT-S3); profile email is 'never readable by anyone but its owner' (§11.2). ARCHITECTURE §14.4: 'there is no path by which an email can reach a subscriber'. GITHUB_PLAN BID-12 makes this its own critical issue (SC-42).

The identity-shaped auction-record fields are opaque identifiers — 'owner identity' (system-assigned at creation from the verified session) and 'winner identity' (outcome, finalization-only) — and neither may be sourced from the auth record. The only public identity attribute anywhere is the profile display name (SEC-P2: 'public user identity is limited to the display name'). For the S0-11 contract this means: no auction-record field may ever hold or join to an email; owner and winner reference profiles whose sole public field is display name.

Ended auctions must remain ordinary, publicly readable rows — 'not archived, moved, hidden, or deleted'; only the listing's read filters by status, and 'a policy that restricted reads by status would break FR-END-12'. This matters to the realtime contract: the Active → Ended broadcast (FR-RT-08) is only deliverable if the Ended row remains readable to every subscriber, anonymous included (§11.2: Anonymous read = all auctions).

Exactly two elevated-privilege operations may write the auction record's derived/outcome fields, and the write scopes are disjoint: 'Bid operation — current price only' and 'Finalization — outcome fields only' (§11.2 auctions table). Each performs its own complete authorization check internally (elevated privilege bypasses RLS), neither accepts a caller-supplied user identifier, and 'any addition to this list is an architectural change'. No user may set current price, status, end time, or winner (SC-40).

The finalization operation must be directly invocable in a test environment without waiting real elapsed time (NFR-MNT-03; repeated verbatim in BID-15's acceptance criteria). Contract consequence: closing is a callable operation taking an auction id, not behavior welded to the scheduler — which is also what T2 (on-read) and T3 (on-bid) presuppose.

The sweep runs inside Supabase, not Vercel (ADR-4: 'a Supabase-side scheduled sweep, plus on-read and on-bid triggers, against one idempotent operation'), and T1 is the correctness guarantee for closure-with-nobody-watching while T2/T3 are latency optimizations ('If T1 fails, auctions still close as soon as anyone interacts ... T1 must be monitored'). ADR-4 is accepted 'pending V-2' — the sub-minute scheduling question of §15.6.

claims.field: current price, final price, starting price
claims.statement: Every amount the closing writes or the projection carries uses the single agreed SAR representation: exact decimal, two places, never floating point (NFR-DAT-05), no maximum (BR-21), one display format everywhere including result views (NFR-DAT-08). ARCHITECTURE §19.2 binds both developers to the S0-12 representation: 'no developer may invent another'.

The realtime projection must be fully reconstructible from a plain read: on reconnect the client re-reads price, history, and status rather than resuming the stream, and 'the page can always reconstruct correct state from a plain read. Realtime is an optimization over refreshing, never a substitute for the authoritative read' (ADR-9: projection, never authority). Duplicate delivery must have no visible effect and price must never appear to move down — so the payload's price/status values must suffice for a monotonic, idempotent client-side merge.

Ownership boundary of the projection at the page: Rayan owns the realtime mechanism and 'decides what is broadcast'; Mohammed's page shell provides the mount points and tells Rayan's components which auction is viewed; the status change 'arrives from Rayan's subscription' into Mohammed's status label; Mohammed 'must not add a second, competing update mechanism'. At close, Mohammed's seller view and Rayan's outcome component 'both read the same recorded result — neither recomputes it' (TEAM 10.5), and the required outcome information for consumers is 'winner identifier and display name, final price, close time, ended status — or an explicit no winner'.

openQuestions: Close-time semantics are never defined: FR-END-08 (PRD.md:689) says 'actual close time' while the bidding cutoff is the immutable end time (LC-03). Since the sweep may run up to 30 s late (or later if only T2/T3 fire), the recorded close time could differ from the end time. The S0-11 contract must state whether the close-time field records the auction's end time or the wall-clock moment finalization ran — Mohammed's seller view (FR-END-13, AUC-17) displays whatever is chosen.

How the winner's display name reaches viewers at close is unsettled. The auction record stores 'winner identity' (an identifier — ARCHITECTURE.md:512, PRD FR-END-08), but TEAM.md:443 (§10.5) says consumers need 'winner identifier and display name', and FR-RT-08 requires the outcome to appear live. A committed-row-change payload cannot join to profiles. Nothing decides between denormalizing the display name onto the auction record at close versus each client resolving identifier → display name from the public profile table.

The same mechanism question exists for live bid history: PRD RT-S1 (PRD.md:1304) lists 'bidder display name' as payload content, but the bid record stores 'bidder identity' (ARCHITECTURE.md:518). How the display name reaches all viewers within the 2-second budget (NFR-RT-01) — denormalized on the bid row, joined server-side, or resolved client-side — is not specified anywhere.

Whether raw account identifiers in payloads comply with RT-S2 is unresolved. RT-S2 (PRD.md:1305) forbids 'internal account identifiers beyond what public display requires', yet ARCHITECTURE §11.2 makes auction rows (including owner and winner identifiers) and bid rows (including bidder identifiers) publicly readable in full, and §14.4 declares payload privacy satisfied 'structurally' by RLS. A raw row-change payload will carry those identifiers. The contract should state explicitly whether identifiers count as 'what public display requires' (because the client needs them to resolve display names) or must be excluded.

The payload shape itself is not fixed: ARCHITECTURE §14.1 says only 'Supabase Realtime detects the committed change'. Whether the projection is a raw postgres-changes row image (all auction columns, all bid columns) or a curated broadcast channel with an agreed field list is undecided — and it determines the answer to the two display-name questions and the RT-S2 question above.

The invocation path for trigger T2 (on-read) is unspecified. ARCHITECTURE §15.3 says T2 finalizes 'before rendering', but finalization is an elevated-privilege operation (§11.4) and a page load is an anonymous RLS read; nothing says whether the detail-page read calls the finalization operation explicitly, and EC-04 (PRD.md:1391) separately tolerates rendering the ended presentation before processing completes ('outcome marked as being finalized'). Whether T2 blocks rendering or runs alongside it needs an agreed answer.

The sweep's 'not yet finalized' predicate is implied (status ≠ Ended, from §15.3 step 2) but never stated as the contract definition of 'finalized'. If the contract instead used close-time-is-null or a separate marker, T1's query and the idempotency guard could diverge. The contract should name status = Ended as the single finalization marker, written atomically with the other three outcome fields.

V-2 (GITHUB_PLAN.md:300, ARCHITECTURE §15.6) is an open verification spike: whether Supabase scheduling achieves ~30 s cadence directly or needs two offset sweeps. It blocks BID-15/R-17 and could alter the sweep configuration (though never the field contract or correctness, per LC-03).

Whether the close broadcast must include close time is unaddressed: ARCHITECTURE §14.3 lists only current price, status, and outcome (winner, final price) as must-deliver; close time is written in the same commit but no requirement says viewers see it live.

claims.statement: Situation 1 of exactly 2: on each accepted bid, Rayan writes current price = the new accepted bid amount. TEAM.md 9.3 'The feedback path': 'Rayan writes back to the auction in exactly two situations... 1. On each accepted bid — the auction's current price becomes the new bid amount. 2. At close...'. GITHUB_PLAN S0-11 AC makes it explicit that 'Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else'.

Transaction for situation 1: the write happens inside the single serialized atomic bid operation, in the SAME transaction as the bid insert — ARCHITECTURE 13.2 steps 8 (append bid) and 9 (update current price) are marked 'inseparable', under an exclusive per-auction row lock acquired in step 2, committed in step 10. ARCHITECTURE 9.4: current price 'is written only by the bid operation, in the same transaction as the bid it derives from (§13). No user, and no other code path, may write it.' Because both writes are one transaction, price can never diverge from history (NFR-DAT-01).

Invariant Rayan maintains: current price always equals the highest accepted bid, or the starting price when there are no bids (BR-13, PRD line 752; ARCHITECTURE.md:535 adds 'zero tolerance' and that it must be independently recomputable from bid history). Rayan does NOT write current price at close — finalization touches outcome fields only (ARCHITECTURE 11.2 auction table: 'Bid operation → current price only; Finalization → outcome fields only').

Initialization is NOT Rayan's write: at publication the current price is set equal to the starting price with an empty bid history, under Mohammed's task M-09 (TEAM.md:595) implementing FR-CREATE-28 (PRD.md:518: 'A newly created auction has a current price equal to its starting price and an empty bid history'). Note a doc tension: ARCHITECTURE 9.3 (line 511) categorizes current price as writable by 'Only the bid operation', which does not mention the creation-time initialization — the contract should record that the initial value belongs to creation (Mohammed), and every subsequent write to it belongs to the bid operation (Rayan).

Situation 2 (close), write 1 of 4: Rayan's finalization operation sets status = Ended. ARCHITECTURE 15.3 finalization box: '1. Lock the auction row; 2. If already Ended → return unchanged; 3. If end time not yet passed → do nothing; 4. Determine highest valid bid; 5. Record: status Ended, final price, winner (or explicitly none), close time; 6. Commit → Realtime broadcasts the change'. The status=Ended write doubles as the idempotency marker (step 2). Ended is terminal: LC-06 'Ended is terminal. Everything recorded at close is permanent'; FR-END-18 forbids reopen/extend/re-run; R-23 enforces no route out of Ended.

Read-side caveat Rayan needs Mohammed to acknowledge: status is in the frozen read set, but bid eligibility is NEVER derived from it. LC-03 (PRD.md:1227): 'Bidding eligibility is determined by server time against the end time, not by the stored status flag. From the end time onward, bids are rejected even if the record still says Active.' ARCHITECTURE 13.2 step 4 checks end time against the DATABASE clock (BR-04, BR-19); ARCHITECTURE 15.2/15.6 restate that a delayed status flip cannot corrupt the outcome. Status is read for presentation and the ended short-circuit only.

Value set for the record: only Active and Ended exist as persisted states. Draft is deliberately not persisted — 'An auction springs into existence Active' (PRD.md:1205, BR-14, FR-CREATE-26/27); there is no Cancelled state (PRD.md:1207, BR-30) and building one is explicitly forbidden (SD-05, PRD.md:392). PRD.md:1245-1247 lists 'a persisted Draft state', 'manual closing', and 'any transition out of Ended' as things that must not exist.

Close with at least one bid: final price = the winning bid amount in SAR (FR-END-09, PRD.md:690), where the winner holds the highest valid bid in history (FR-END-05, BR-06). Since BR-13 keeps current price = highest accepted bid, final price necessarily equals the current price at the moment of close when bids exist — but it is read from bid history inside the finalization transaction (ARCHITECTURE 15.7: 'Read from the recorded bid history inside the finalization transaction'), not copied by assumption.

Close with NO bids: there is NO final price. FR-END-09 (PRD.md:690): 'where there were no bids — the auction ends with no final price and the starting price is retained for display only.' BR-09 (PRD.md:748): zero bids ends with 'no winner and no final sale price'. EC-05 (PRD.md:1392): closes normally with no winner and no final price; 'a normal outcome, never an error state, and must not block or delay close processing.' Concretely: final price is left empty/absent, NOT set to the starting price; the current-price field (still = starting price) is what display falls back to.

Determination rule: highest valid bid in history wins (BR-06); theoretical ties resolved to the earlier-ordered bid (FR-END-06, in practice unreachable since equal accepted bids are prevented); exactly once and idempotent (BR-17, FR-END-10, EC-19); no reserve check — exactly two outcomes exist, 'a winner, or no bids — never a third' (ARCHITECTURE 15.2 and 15.7). The recorded winner must equal the highest bidder in history for 100% of closed auctions, verifiable by independent recomputation (NFR-DAT-04, SC-29).

Representation: the documents point to a USER REFERENCE (internal identifier), rendered as a display name, never stored as a name string and never an email. Evidence: BR-39 rationale (PRD.md:778) and A-T4/Q11 (PRD.md:1955, 2006): 'The internal identifier remains the source of truth for attribution'; FR-PROF-05 (PRD.md:466): display-name edits 'must not retroactively alter historical bid records' attribution' (a stored name string would break this and would break the SC-29 recomputation check, which compares against bid history attribution); TEAM 10.5 (TEAM.md:443) names the consumer's required information as 'Winner identifier AND display name'; the views then show the display name (FR-DETAIL-18 PRD.md:557, FR-END-13 PRD.md:694).

'Explicitly none' concretely: the winner field is nullable/none-capable, and the no-winner outcome is affirmatively RECORDED, not merely left unprocessed. FR-END-07 (PRD.md:688): 'ends with no winner and is recorded as such'; FR-END-08 (PRD.md:689): 'winner identity (or explicitly none)'; TEAM 10.5 (TEAM.md:443): 'or an explicit "no winner" when the auction closed with zero bids'. What makes 'none' explicit rather than 'not yet': status = Ended plus close time are written in the same finalization transaction (ARCHITECTURE 15.3 step 5), and the already-Ended check (step 2) is the marker that finalization ran — so Ended + empty winner is a recorded no-winner outcome, while not-Ended + empty winner is simply unfinalized.

Privacy constraint on the field's downstream use: BR-26 (PRD.md:765) — identities shown by display name only, emails never public; FR-BID-22a (PRD.md:645) — display names only, 'never email addresses, never internal identifiers' in PUBLIC history display; realtime payloads must carry only publicly visible data, never emails (TEAM.md:433 per RT-S2; ARCHITECTURE 14.4 satisfies this structurally because emails live only in the auth record). The outcome broadcast at close (winner, final price, status) rides the same auction-record change (ARCHITECTURE 14.3, lines 957-958), so the winner value in that payload must be safe to expose.

Written at close inside the finalization transaction as one of the four outcome fields. FR-END-08 (PRD.md:689) calls it the 'actual close time'. Once recorded it is immutable: SEC-I2 (PRD.md:1346): 'Once recorded, an auction outcome — winner, final price, close time — must be immutable (BR-17)'; LC-06 makes everything recorded at close permanent. R-21 (TEAM.md:650) is the owning task: 'Outcome recording — ended status, close time, final price, winner (or explicitly none), permanently and immutably'.

Close transaction shape: finalization is ONE idempotent, transactional operation (lock auction row → return unchanged if already Ended → do nothing if end time not passed → determine highest valid bid from history → record all four outcome fields → commit, and the commit itself triggers the realtime broadcast). It is invoked by three triggers — T1 scheduled sweep (the correctness guarantee for FR-END-02/SC-26, recommended as a Supabase in-database scheduled job, ADR-4), T2 on-read, T3 on-bid-attempt — and all three may fire for the same auction with no ill effect because of idempotency. Deadline is the end time recorded at creation, never extended (BR-36).

Bid transaction shape: a single serialized atomic database operation is the ONLY path that can insert a bid (direct insert denied to every user role — ADR-2, ARCHITECTURE 11.2 bids table, 'the load-bearing decision'). In one transaction: verify auth from session (never payload) → exclusive lock on THIS auction row → re-read auction state INSIDE the lock (stale-before-lock data must not be used) → end time vs database clock → caller is not owner → amount well-formed (numeric, > 0, at most two decimals, NO maximum check) → minimum acceptable bid → append bid + update current price (inseparable) → commit, releasing the lock so the next bid evaluates against the state this one produced (BR-11). Rejection aborts before any write (BR-23) and must return a specific reason, including the distinguishable 'lost a concurrent race' case.

Minimum acceptable bid — the exact rule bid validation applies against the read fields: no bids yet → amount >= starting price (INCLUSIVE; a first bid exactly equal to the starting price is accepted, SC-55); has bids → amount > current price (STRICT; the same amount is rejected and that amount + 0.01 SAR is accepted, SC-56). ARCHITECTURE 13.2a: 'The whole amount rule is BR-28, and it has exactly two branches... Anything else is not a rule of this product.' The four checks that must NOT exist: bid increment (BR-32), maximum amount (BR-21), leading-bidder (BR-24), reserve price (BR-35) — adding any back is a bug (SD-05).

How the 'has bids' branch is decided — a contract point Mohammed must confirm: it CANNOT be inferred by comparing current price to starting price, because after SC-55 (first bid exactly equal to starting price) the two are equal while the auction HAS a bid, and SC-56 requires rejecting a repeat of that amount — a price-comparison shortcut would wrongly accept it. ARCHITECTURE 13.2 step 3 re-reads 'owner, status, end time, current price, bid count' inside the lock, i.e. the branch comes from actual bid existence. Whether that count is derived from bid history or stored anywhere is not settled (see open questions).

The read-set lists disagree across documents and the contract must record the reconciled union. GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 (S0-11 AC): six fields = auction id, owner, status, end time, starting price, CURRENT PRICE. TEAM.md:421 (§10.3) and TEAM.md:372 (§9.3): six = auction ID, owner identifier, status, end time, starting price, 'whether the auction exists' — current price absent. Yet TEAM.md:369, in the same §9.3 table, says BR-03 'needs the current price and starting price', and ARCHITECTURE.md:1295 lists the fields the bid operation reads as 'owner, status, end time, starting price, current price'. Union Rayan actually needs to read: auction id, existence, owner identifier, status, end time, starting price, current price. The freeze rule ('renaming or removing any requires telling Rayan first', TEAM.md:422, GITHUB_PLAN.md:263) must cover current price.

Write exclusivity and privilege: exactly two elevated operations exist — bid acceptance and finalization (ARCHITECTURE 11.4: 'Any addition to this list is an architectural change'). On the auction record: bid operation may update current price ONLY; finalization may update outcome fields ONLY; no user, including the owner, has any update or delete right (immutable BR-31, no cancel BR-30). SEC-Z5/Z6/Z7 (PRD.md:1329-1330 via mapping at ARCHITECTURE.md:705-707): no user may set current price, set/claim a winner, or change status/end time. SC-40 (PRD.md:1678) requires an automated test PER FIELD: 'A user cannot set an auction's current price, status, end time, or winner directly.' Each elevated operation performs its own complete authorization check and never accepts a caller-supplied user identifier.

Money representation for every price field Rayan reads or writes (starting price read; current price, final price, bid amounts written): SAR, exact decimal, exactly two places, NEVER floating point, exact at any magnitude because there is NO maximum (NFR-DAT-05, BR-21), one display format everywhere (NFR-DAT-08), values simulated (BR-33), 'Demo Points' prohibited. One representation agreed once in S0-12; no developer may invent another (TEAM.md:487). SC-56's '+0.01 SAR is accepted' makes exact two-decimal comparison correctness-critical in the bid operation, which is why S0-12 assigns the comparison half to Rayan.

What close does NOT touch: bid history is preserved unchanged, permanently, through and after the transition (FR-END-11 PRD.md:692, LC-07 PRD.md:1231); bids are append-only with no update or delete path for any user including bidder and seller (SC-15 PRD.md:1628, BID-01 GITHUB_PLAN.md:444); current price is not rewritten at close (GITHUB_PLAN.md:263: current price on each accepted bid 'and nothing else'; ARCHITECTURE.md:675: finalization → outcome fields only). Rayan writes to the auction record in exactly two situations and 'no other write from Rayan to the auction record is permitted without coordinating with Mohammed' (TEAM.md:381); the close fields are agreed in Sprint 0, 'added once, and not renegotiated mid-sprint' (TEAM.md:374).

Documentation cross-reference bug worth flagging when this contract is recorded: GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 cites 'ARCHITECTURE §10.3' twice for the auction-record contract, but ARCHITECTURE §10.3 is 'Password reset' (ARCHITECTURE.md:605); the content actually lives in TEAM.md §10.3 (TEAM.md:415) and ARCHITECTURE §9.3/§9.4/§19.3 (ARCHITECTURE.md:501, 529, 1295). Since all three developers build via separate Claude sessions reading these documents, a wrong pointer will send a session to the wrong section.

openQuestions: Concrete representation of 'explicitly none': the semantics are settled (status Ended + close time written, winner and final price affirmatively absent — FR-END-07/08, BR-09), but no document specifies whether winner and final price are nullable columns, a separate flag, or a sentinel. This must be recorded as part of the S0-11 agreement, not inferred independently by three Claude sessions (TEAM.md rule 16, TEAM.md:1156).

What 'actual close time' (FR-END-08, PRD.md:689) records: the auction's end time (the moment bidding actually ceased per LC-03), or the database timestamp when finalization committed. With the ≤30 s sweep these differ by seconds, but under T2/T3-only closing (sweep failure) they could differ substantially. No document settles which value is written.

Who mechanically initializes current price at creation: FR-CREATE-28 (PRD.md:518) and M-09 (TEAM.md:595) put 'current price = starting price, empty history' in Mohammed's publication behavior, while ARCHITECTURE.md:511 says current price is writable by 'Only the bid operation'. Whether the initial value is a column default in Mohammed's record definition or an explicit write in his creation flow is unsettled; either way it must not become a path Rayan uses.

Whether the 'bid count' that ARCHITECTURE.md:817 re-reads inside the bid lock is derived from bid history or stored on the auction record. If stored, someone must write it on every accepted bid — contradicting the S0-11 AC that Rayan writes 'current price on each accepted bid and nothing else' (GITHUB_PLAN.md:263). Deriving it from history inside the transaction keeps the AC intact; needs joint confirmation with Mohammed.

Which six-field read list is canonical for the frozen S0-11 record: GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 includes current price but not existence; TEAM.md:372/421 include existence but not current price. Both are needed (TEAM.md:369 itself says BR-03 reads current price; existence is rejection reason 'Auction not found', ARCHITECTURE.md:898). The joint agreement should record the seven-item union explicitly so the rename/removal freeze covers all of them.

Whether T3 (finalization triggered by a bid attempt arriving after end time, ARCHITECTURE.md:1039-1045) runs inside the same database call as the bid rejection or as a separate follow-up invocation. Idempotency makes either safe, but the bid operation's own contract (reject → abort with no writes, BR-23) suggests finalization is a separate call — not stated anywhere.

The exact stored form of the status value ('Active'/'Ended' strings, an enum type, etc.) and field naming are Mohammed's to propose as record owner; the documents constrain the value set (only Active and Ended persist) but not the representation.

claims.statement: The issue of record for this contract, S0-11, freezes exactly six read fields for bid validation — auction id, owner, status, end time, starting price, current price — plus four fields Rayan writes at close (status, final price, winner, close time), and makes explicit that 'Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else'. Renaming or removing any of the six requires telling Rayan first.

TEAM.md carries a conflicting six-field list: section 10.3 names 'Auction ID, owner identifier, status, end time, starting price, and whether the auction exists' (TEAM.md:421), and section 9.3 'What is shared' repeats it (TEAM.md:372) — current price is absent from both. Yet the same 9.3 table's 'Why it exists' row states BR-03 'needs the current price and starting price' (TEAM.md:369), and ARCHITECTURE.md:1295 lists the bid-operation read fields as 'owner, status, end time, starting price, current price'. Three of the four listings plus BR-03's own justification require current price in the read set; only TEAM.md's shared-list wording omits it.

'Whether the auction exists' (TEAM.md:421) is not a stored field — it is the outcome of the id lookup. ARCHITECTURE 13.2 step 4 checks 'Auction exists and end time has not passed' (ARCHITECTURE.md:820), and 13.5 requires a distinct 'Auction not found' rejection reason (ARCHITECTURE.md:898). The contract needs a lookup that can fail distinguishably, not a column.

Consumed at 13.2 step 2 as the row-lock key: 'Acquire an exclusive lock on THIS auction row' — the lock is per-auction so bids on different auctions never block each other (ARCHITECTURE.md:811-814, 873-875). Non-null by construction (it is the key); a failed lookup is the 'Auction not found' rejection, not a NULL. Concrete type is unspecified — ARCHITECTURE.md:480 says 'No SQL, no types, no migrations'. It must be stable and passable: Mohammed's page mounts Rayan's components and passes them the auction ID (TEAM.md:505).

Consumed at 13.2 step 5: 'Caller is not the auction owner — BR-02' (ARCHITECTURE.md:823). PRD BR-02: 'The auction creator cannot bid on their own auction', enforced server on every bid (PRD.md:736). Step 5 is an equality comparison between the auction's owner and the caller's verified identity, so the owner field's TYPE must be identical to the server-side verified identifier defined in the S0-10 identity contract — 'the authenticated user identifier as the database sees it' (GITHUB_PLAN.md:262). NULLABILITY: must be NOT NULL — BR-10 'An auction has exactly one owner, set at creation and never transferable' (PRD.md:749), LC-09 (PRD.md:1233), and it is system-assigned from the verified session at creation (ARCHITECTURE.md:510). A NULL would mean an ownerless auction, violating BR-10 and making the BR-02 check undecidable (in SQL, caller = NULL evaluates to neither true nor false, silently letting the owner bid). Must be impossible at the schema level.

Status is READ but is NOT the bid-eligibility gate. It appears in the 13.2 step-3 re-read list ('owner, status, end time, current price, bid count', ARCHITECTURE.md:817) and in every frozen-six listing, yet NO validation step of 13.2 consumes it: step 4 gates on 'end time has not passed — compared against the DATABASE clock' (ARCHITECTURE.md:820-821, BR-04/BR-19). PRD LC-03 is explicit: 'Bidding eligibility is determined by server time against the end time, not by the stored status flag. From the end time onward, bids are rejected even if the record still says Active' (PRD.md:1227). Corroborated by FR-BID-18 (PRD.md:637), SC-27 (PRD.md:1655), BID-13's AC 'A bid at or after the end time is always rejected — even if the record still says Active' (GITHUB_PLAN.md:456), R-18 (TEAM.md:647), and R-03's own phrasing 'auction Active by server time' (TEAM.md:632). ARCHITECTURE.md:1076 restates it: 'bid rejection is driven by the auction's actual end timestamp compared against the database clock — never by the stored status flag.'

The converse direction also cannot make status load-bearing: a row can never be Ended while its end time is in the future. Finalization step 3 says 'If end time not yet passed → do nothing' (ARCHITECTURE.md:1030), the only Active→Ended transition trigger is 'Server time reaches or passes the end time' (PRD.md:1214, T2), and 'No manual transitions. No user, including the seller, can change status directly' (PRD.md:1221, FR-SEC-08; SC-40 PRD.md:1678). Therefore end-time-vs-database-clock is sufficient AND necessary as the sole gate, and status is display/idempotency state from the bid operation's perspective.

TYPE domain: exactly two persisted values, Active and Ended. PRD 12.1: 'The MVP has two operative states, plus a conceptual state that is not persisted' — Draft is 'No — conceptual only' (PRD.md:1196-1200) and 'Cancelled | Does not exist' (PRD.md:1203, BR-30; SD-05 PRD.md:392 forbids introducing a Cancelled state). NULLABILITY: must be NOT NULL — set Active at creation (BR-14 PRD.md:753, FR-CREATE-26 PRD.md:516); no third state exists, so a NULL has no defined meaning anywhere in the lifecycle. The concrete representation (two-valued enum vs text vs boolean) is not specified by any document.

Consumed at 13.2 step 4: 'end time has not passed — compared against the DATABASE clock' (ARCHITECTURE.md:820-821; BR-04 PRD.md:738, BR-19 PRD.md:758 'All time-based decisions use authoritative server time; client clocks are display-only'). This is the SOLE eligibility gate (LC-03). TYPE: a timestamp; 'One canonical zone stored; server clock authoritative; local display' (ARCHITECTURE.md:1284, BR-19/FR-CREATE-14); validated at creation to 5 minutes–7 days ahead inclusive against server time (GITHUB_PLAN.md:370, AUC-02/BR-38/SC-68). NULLABILITY: must be NOT NULL — it is one of the five required creation fields (GITHUB_PLAN.md:369, AUC-01/FR-CREATE-01/03), immutable after creation (BR-16 PRD.md:1219, SEC-Z7, SC-40 PRD.md:1678, no anti-sniping BR-36 ARCHITECTURE.md:1020). A NULL would make every bid's eligibility undecidable (step 4 cannot evaluate) AND make the auction unclosable, since the T1 sweep 'finds auctions past their end time' (ARCHITECTURE.md:1040-1043) — an auction that can never end violates the entire lifecycle. Must be impossible.

Consumed at 13.2 step 7, no-bids branch only: 'no bids yet → amount >= starting price — BR-29' (ARCHITECTURE.md:829-830); BR-28: 'the starting price inclusive when the auction has no bids' (PRD.md:767); SC-55: a first bid of exactly the starting price is accepted (PRD.md:1623). Also needed to compose the rejection message 'Bidding starts at X SAR' (ARCHITECTURE.md:902). NOTE: starting price is absent from the step-3 re-read list (ARCHITECTURE.md:817) — this is safe only because it is immutable ('User-supplied at creation, then immutable', ARCHITECTURE.md:509, BR-31), so a pre-lock read cannot be stale; the contract should state this immutability as the justification. NULLABILITY: NOT NULL — required creation field, validated '> 0, two decimals, in SAR' with no maximum (GITHUB_PLAN.md:369-370, FR-CREATE-07 PRD.md:486). A NULL would make the first-bid minimum (BR-28/BR-29) undecidable.

Consumed at 13.2 step 7, has-bids branch: 'has bids → amount > current price — BR-03' (ARCHITECTURE.md:831; BR-28 PRD.md:767 'strictly greater'; SC-56 PRD.md:1624: an equal bid is rejected, +0.01 SAR accepted). MUST be the value re-read INSIDE the row lock — 'Anything read before the lock is already stale' (ARCHITECTURE.md:816-818); this staleness rule is what makes BR-12 hold (ARCHITECTURE.md:852). Also read on the rejection path to compose 'Your bid must be higher than X SAR' and 'Someone bid before you — the current price is now X SAR' (ARCHITECTURE.md:903-904), while a rejection changes nothing (BR-23, ARCHITECTURE.md:856). NULLABILITY: NOT NULL from creation — FR-CREATE-28: 'A newly created auction has a current price equal to its starting price and an empty bid history' (PRD.md:518; M-09 TEAM.md:595; T1 effects PRD.md:1213), and BR-13 gives it a total definition: 'always the highest accepted bid; before any bid it is the starting price' (PRD.md:752). A NULL would violate BR-13 and break step 7. In particular, a design that encodes 'no bids yet' as NULL current price is ruled out by FR-CREATE-28. Written only by the bid operation, in the same transaction as the bid (BR-07 PRD.md:741, SC-40 PRD.md:1678, ARCHITECTURE.md:511, 534, 674).

Step 7 branches on 'no bids yet' vs 'has bids' (ARCHITECTURE.md:829-831), and step 3 re-reads 'bid count' inside the lock (ARCHITECTURE.md:817) — yet bid count appears in NO frozen-six list (GITHUB_PLAN.md:263, TEAM.md:421, ARCHITECTURE.md:1295). Critically, has-bids CANNOT be inferred from current price == starting price: per SC-55/SC-56 (PRD.md:1623-1624), after a first bid of exactly 100 SAR on a 100 SAR start, current price equals starting price while the auction HAS a bid, and a second 100 SAR bid must be rejected. Any contract that derives 'no bids' from price equality accepts that second bid and fails SC-56. The determinant must therefore come from bid existence itself. The documents do not settle where it lives (see open questions).

Both prices share ONE representation, agreed in S0-12 and used by everyone: 'exact decimal, two places, never floating point' (NFR-DAT-05 PRD.md:1546; S0-12 AC GITHUB_PLAN.md:264; TEAM.md:474), with NO maximum — 'large values must also be stored, compared, and displayed exactly — precision must not degrade at scale' (NFR-DAT-05 PRD.md:1546; BR-21 PRD.md:760; SEC-R3), and one display format everywhere (NFR-DAT-08 PRD.md:1547). TEAM.md:466 states why this is correctness-critical for the bid operation: 'a rounding mismatch between the price a bidder sees and the price the server validates against is a correctness bug'. Consequences for the contract: the step-7 comparisons are exact-decimal comparisons; a floating-point column is forbidden; and a fixed-width integer-cents representation with a hard ceiling conflicts with the no-maximum + no-precision-degradation pair. S0-12 is assigned to Rayan precisely because 'the correctness-critical half — exact comparison in the bid operation — is his' (GITHUB_PLAN.md:264).

Fields the contract must NOT contain and the bid operation must NOT read: ARCHITECTURE 13.2a lists four checks whose addition is a bug — bid increment (BR-32), maximum amount (BR-21/SEC-R3), leading-bidder status (BR-24/FR-BID-04), reserve price (BR-35) (ARCHITECTURE.md:860-869). 'The whole amount rule is BR-28... Anything else is not a rule of this product' (ARCHITECTURE.md:871). AUC-01's AC independently requires 'no reserve-price field' on the record (GITHUB_PLAN.md:369), PRD SD-05 forbids introducing any of these (PRD.md:392), and ARCHITECTURE risk 10 flags re-adding a removed check as a named failure mode requiring explicit code-review attention (ARCHITECTURE.md:1451). Rayan's half of S0-11 should state affirmatively that he needs NO increment, ceiling, leading-bidder, or reserve field — so Mohammed does not add one 'to be helpful'.

Step-by-step field consumption of ARCHITECTURE 13.2 (lines 804-844): Step 1 (authenticate, BR-01) — no auction field; identity from session, never the payload. Step 2 (exclusive row lock) — auction id. Step 3 (re-read inside lock) — owner, status, end time, current price, bid count. Step 4 (exists + end time not passed, BR-04/BR-19) — existence outcome + end time vs database clock; NOT status. Step 5 (caller not owner, BR-02) — owner. Step 6 (amount well-formed: numeric, > 0, at most two decimals, no maximum, BR-21/FR-BID-07) — no auction field. Step 7 (minimum acceptable bid, BR-28) — has-bids determinant, then starting price (no-bids branch, >=) or current price (has-bids branch, >); explicitly no increment/leading/reserve logic. Step 8 (append bid, BR-18) — write to bids, not a read of the auction. Step 9 (update current price, BR-13) — the single auction write, inseparable from step 8. Step 10 — commit; the next bid evaluates against the state this one produced (BR-11).

Freshness rule for the contract: every MUTABLE field consumed for a decision must be the value re-read inside the per-auction row lock — 'Anything read before the lock is already stale' (ARCHITECTURE.md:816-818); this is what satisfies BR-12 (ARCHITECTURE.md:852) and resolves the 13.1 lost-bid scenario (ARCHITECTURE.md:858). Only immutable fields (starting price, end time — ARCHITECTURE.md:509) are safe to read pre-lock, though end time is listed in the re-read anyway. The lock is on THIS auction row only, so bids on different auctions never queue behind each other (ARCHITECTURE.md:873-875).

The bid operation writes exactly ONE auction field: current price, in the same transaction as the history append — 'steps 8 and 9 are inseparable' (ARCHITECTURE.md:838-840; NFR-DAT-01 ARCHITECTURE.md:855). The RLS access model grants the bid operation 'current price only' on auctions (ARCHITECTURE.md:674) and the finalization operation 'outcome fields only' (ARCHITECTURE.md:675). S0-11's AC makes this contractual: 'Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else' (GITHUB_PLAN.md:263; TEAM.md:376-381 lists the only two write-back situations). The four close fields (status, final price, winner, close time — FR-END-08 PRD.md:689) are written by finalization (ARCHITECTURE.md:1031-1033), NOT by the bid operation, and the bid operation reads none of them.

Privacy scope of the read contract: the owner field the bid operation reads is an internal IDENTIFIER only — never an email (BR-26 PRD.md:765: 'email addresses are never public'; ARCHITECTURE.md:497: never visible 'anywhere, including in realtime payloads'; TEAM.md:433: 'display names, never email addresses'). Public bid history additionally shows 'display names only — never email addresses, never internal identifiers' (FR-BID-22a PRD.md:645), so the owner identifier read for BR-02 must not leak into history payloads either. Display names come from the separate profile entity (ARCHITECTURE.md:497-499), not from the auction record — the contract should not ask Mohammed to denormalize seller name or email onto the auction row.

Rejection-reason granularity constrains the read set: ARCHITECTURE 13.5 requires the operation to distinguish eight reasons, several of which embed a price value in the message — 'Bidding starts at X SAR' (starting price), 'Your bid must be higher than X SAR' (current price), 'Someone bid before you — the current price is now X SAR' (post-race current price, distinguishable from a plain too-low bid) (ARCHITECTURE.md:893-906; BR-27, FR-BID-13, EC-01; SC-13/SC-18 via GITHUB_PLAN.md:447). So starting price and current price are read even on rejection paths, while BR-23 requires the rejection to change nothing (ARCHITECTURE.md:856; GITHUB_PLAN.md:447: 'a rejection leaves auction state entirely unchanged and adds nothing to history').

Guard against a known shorthand misreading: TEAM.md R-03's row abbreviates the amount rule as 'strictly greater than current price' (TEAM.md:632), but TEAM.md's own finalized-decisions table for Rayan restores the full rule: 'First bid may equal the starting price — an explicit special case in R-03. Starting price 100 SAR → a first bid of 100 SAR is valid; a second bid of 100 SAR is not' (TEAM.md:662, BR-29/FR-BID-06). Rayan's half of the contract should quote BR-28's two-branch form verbatim so neither Mohammed's session nor a reviewer treats the R-03 shorthand as the rule.

The same inclusive/exclusive distinction must also be computable OUTSIDE the bid operation, for display: BID-06 requires 'Bidding starts at 100 SAR' with no bids vs 'Enter more than 250 SAR' once bidding has begun (GITHUB_PLAN.md:449; FR-BID-10 PRD.md:623; NFR-USA-11), and Mohammed's AUC-14 price region must distinguish 'Starting price: 100 SAR (no bids yet)' from 'Current bid: 250 SAR' and make clear a first bid of exactly the starting price is acceptable (GITHUB_PLAN.md:382; FR-DETAIL-06 PRD.md:545). So whatever form the has-bids fact takes in the contract, both the server operation and both developers' UI read paths need it — another reason S0-11 must name its home explicitly.

Process constraint on this deliverable: TEAM.md rule 16 — 'PRD.md contains the finalized MVP product decisions... If a genuinely new ambiguity is discovered during implementation, it must be raised with the team rather than silently invented' (TEAM.md:1156; reiterated TEAM.md:1288 and risk 4 TEAM.md:1196). The items below in openQuestions are therefore stated as questions for Mohammed/the team, not answered unilaterally. The contract, once agreed, is frozen: 'treat it as frozen once agreed' (TEAM.md:422), 'Frozen once agreed' (ARCHITECTURE.md:1295), 'added once, and not renegotiated mid-sprint' (TEAM.md:374).

openQuestions: Where does the has-bids/bid-count fact live? ARCHITECTURE.md:817 (13.2 step 3) re-reads 'bid count' as part of auction state inside the lock, but bid count is in NO frozen-six list (GITHUB_PLAN.md:263, TEAM.md:421, ARCHITECTURE.md:1295). Two doc-consistent designs exist: (a) a bid-count/has-bids column on Mohammed's auction record — but then S0-11's AC 'Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else' (GITHUB_PLAN.md:263) must be amended, since accepting a bid would have to update it; or (b) Rayan derives it inside the lock from his own bids table (he owns the bid entity, ARCHITECTURE.md:489; BID-01 GITHUB_PLAN.md:444), which fits 'each fact has exactly one authoritative home... Nothing is stored in two places' (ARCHITECTURE.md:493) and keeps the auction contract at six fields. The documents do not decide. Note it can NOT be derived from current price == starting price (SC-55/SC-56, PRD.md:1623-1624).

Which six-field list is canonical for the S0-11 sign-off text: GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 (id, owner, status, end time, starting price, CURRENT PRICE) or TEAM.md:372/421 (…, 'whether the auction exists', no current price)? All the operational evidence (TEAM.md:369's own BR-03 justification, ARCHITECTURE.md:831 step 7, ARCHITECTURE.md:1295, ARCH §9.4) requires current price in the read set and treats existence as a lookup outcome, but no document formally supersedes the TEAM.md wording. Mohammed should confirm the GITHUB_PLAN.md list in writing so three Claude sessions don't resolve the discrepancy three ways.

Concrete PostgreSQL types and explicit NOT NULL constraints are specified nowhere — ARCHITECTURE.md:480 deliberately says 'No SQL, no types, no migrations'. The docs fix only the constraint envelope: money = exact decimal, two places, never floating point, no ceiling, no precision loss at scale (NFR-DAT-05, BR-21); end time = timestamp in one agreed canonical zone (ARCHITECTURE.md:1284); owner id type = identical to the S0-10 server-side verified identifier; status = two-valued. The actual column types (e.g. id: UUID vs other; status: enum vs text; NUMERIC precision/scale choice) and the canonical timezone convention are Mohammed's to propose and must be recorded in S0-11/S0-12 — every nullability statement in the claims above is DERIVED from creation rules and invariants, never stated as NULL/NOT NULL in any document, so the agreed contract should write the NOT NULLs down explicitly.

Does the bid operation use status for anything at all? It is in the 13.2 step-3 re-read list and the frozen six, yet no validation step consumes it and LC-03 forbids gating on it. Plausible uses the docs hint at but never assign to the bid operation: deciding whether to fire finalization trigger T3 when a bid arrives after the end time (ARCHITECTURE.md:1039-1043 says the bid is rejected 'and finalization triggered' but does not say whether the bid operation itself checks status or calls finalization, or whether that call is inside or after its transaction), and shaping the 'auction has ended' response (ARCHITECTURE.md:899). Mohammed and Rayan should agree whether status is contractually read-for-display/trigger only, or can be dropped from the bid operation's read set entirely — either way the field stays in the record because Rayan writes it at close.

PRD FR-END-09 (PRD.md:690) says a zero-bid auction 'ends with no final price and the starting price is retained for display only' — this entails final price and winner are absent (explicitly none) on a no-bid close (BR-09, TEAM.md:443: 'an explicit "no winner"'). How 'explicitly none' is represented (NULLs + Ended status + close time, vs a separate marker) is not specified anywhere; it is outside the bid operation's read set but inside the four close-write fields of S0-11, so the representation of 'no winner / no final price' must be agreed in the same conversation.

contradictions.topic: The has-bids determinant: BR-28's two-branch rule requires the bid operation to know whether any bid exists, but no frozen field list contains that fact, no document assigns it a home or a writer, and the S0-11 contract text forbids maintaining it as a stored field
contradictions.sideA: GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 (S0-11 AC): "the six read fields are defined and frozen: auction id, owner, status, end time, starting price, current price · ... it is explicit that Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else" — no bid-count/has-bids field, and the 'nothing else' clause forbids Rayan writing one. TEAM.md:595 (M-09): publication sets "current price = starting price, empty history", so on a fresh auction current price EQUALS starting price.
contradictions.sideB: ARCHITECTURE.md:817 (13.2 step 3) re-reads "owner, status, end time, current price, bid count" inside the lock, and ARCHITECTURE.md:829-831 (step 7) branches: "no bids yet → amount >= starting price (BR-29); has bids → amount > current price (BR-03)". PRD.md:767 (BR-28), PRD.md:1623 (SC-55: first bid of exactly 100 SAR on a 100 SAR start is ACCEPTED), PRD.md:1624 (SC-56: a second 100 SAR bid is REJECTED, 100.01 accepted). "bid count" appears exactly once in all four documents (grep-verified) — never in ARCHITECTURE §9.3's field table (505-512), never in any frozen list (GITHUB_PLAN.md:263, TEAM.md:372/421, ARCHITECTURE.md:1295), never initialized by M-09.
contradictions.whyItMatters: This is the trap the task flagged, and it is real. A developer implementing strictly from the frozen six fields has only current price to compare against; since M-09 initializes current price = starting price, the naive 'amount > current price' (which is exactly how TEAM.md:632 R-03 abbreviates the rule: "strictly greater than current price") REJECTS the first bid equal to the starting price — SC-55 fails and the product contradicts its own price label (BR-29 rationale). The obvious repair — infer 'no bids' from current price == starting price — fails the other direction: after SC-55's first bid the two are equal while the auction HAS a bid, so a second equal bid is wrongly ACCEPTED and SC-56 fails, breaking BR-12 (one bid per price level) and potentially producing two claimants at the same price. The third repair — a stored bid_count column Rayan updates on each accepted bid — directly violates the S0-11 AC 'current price on each accepted bid and nothing else'. Every path a session can take from the written contract is wrong. The same fact is separately required for display labels (FR-DETAIL-06 PRD.md:545, FR-LIST-03 PRD.md:525), so up to three sessions will each invent a different mechanism.
contradictions.recommendation: The documents DO provide a doc-consistent escape, but only implicitly: Rayan owns the Bid entity (ARCHITECTURE.md:489) and the bid operation already runs inside a transaction holding the auction row lock, so 'bid count' should be DERIVED in-transaction from the bids table (an EXISTS check on bids for this auction, inside the lock), not stored on the auction record. This keeps the contract at six fields, keeps 'nothing else' intact, and honors "each fact has exactly one authoritative home... Nothing is stored in two places" (ARCHITECTURE.md:493). Rayan's half of S0-11 must state this explicitly: (1) the BR-28 branch is decided by bid existence read from the bids table inside the bid transaction — never by price equality (quote SC-55/SC-56 verbatim); (2) no bid-count column is requested on the auction record; (3) the display-side 'no bids yet' state (FR-DETAIL-06/FR-LIST-03) is likewise derived from bid-history emptiness, supplied through Rayan's components/read path, and Mohammed must not compute it from price comparison. Mohammed must confirm in writing.

contradictions.topic: The sixth frozen read field: GITHUB_PLAN says current price, TEAM.md says 'whether the auction exists' (current price absent), ARCHITECTURE has a third five-field variant — and TEAM.md contradicts itself within one table
contradictions.sideA: GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 (S0-11 AC): "the six read fields are defined and frozen: auction id, owner, status, end time, starting price, current price". Corroborated by ARCHITECTURE.md:831 (step 7 reads current price for BR-03), ARCHITECTURE.md:953 (§14.3: current price broadcast sourced from "Auction record change"), and TEAM.md:369 itself: "BR-03 (bid must be higher) needs the current price and starting price".
contradictions.sideB: TEAM.md:421 (§10.3 Required information): "Auction ID, owner identifier, status, end time, starting price, and whether the auction exists" — current price absent; TEAM.md:422 then freezes it: "does not rename or remove any of the six fields above without telling Rayan first... treat it as frozen once agreed". TEAM.md:372 (§9.3 What is shared) repeats the same list: "Auction ID · auction owner identifier · auction status · auction end time · starting price · existence of the auction" — three lines after TEAM.md:369 said BR-03 needs current price. A third variant exists at ARCHITECTURE.md:1295: "Auction fields the bid operation reads: owner, status, end time, starting price, current price. Frozen once agreed (TEAM.md §10.3, M-01)" — five fields, no id, no existence, while citing as its source the very TEAM.md section that lists a different set.
contradictions.whyItMatters: This is the sign-off text of the contract itself, and there are three incompatible versions of it. If Mohammed's session freezes the TEAM.md:421 list, his access path need not expose current price to Rayan — making BR-03/step 7 unimplementable through the sanctioned path, and forcing Rayan to either write his own auction query (forbidden: TEAM.md:373 "he does not write his own auction queries"; TEAM.md:422 "Rayan reads only through Mohammed's access path") or stall. It also breaks the realtime must-deliver (ARCHITECTURE.md:953 requires the price change to ride the auction record change — impossible if the field is not part of the shared record contract). Conversely, 'whether the auction exists' is genuinely needed (the distinct "Auction not found" rejection, ARCHITECTURE.md:898) and is absent from the GITHUB_PLAN list, so freezing only that list loses the existence guarantee.
contradictions.recommendation: GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 wins on the disputed slot — the operational evidence is unanimous (TEAM.md:369, ARCHITECTURE.md:831, ARCHITECTURE.md:953, ARCHITECTURE.md:1295 all require current price in the read set) and 'whether the auction exists' is not a field at all but the outcome of the id lookup (ARCHITECTURE.md:820 step 4 'Auction exists', ARCHITECTURE.md:898 distinct not-found rejection). Rayan's half should record the reconciled contract explicitly: six FIELDS (auction id, owner, status, end time, starting price, current price) PLUS the guarantee that the lookup by id can fail distinguishably ('Auction not found'). The freeze/rename rule must cover all of it, current price included. Ask Mohammed to confirm this union in writing in the S0-11 issue and to fix TEAM.md:372/421 so the three Claude sessions stop resolving the discrepancy three ways.

contradictions.topic: Who initializes current price at creation: ARCHITECTURE's write matrix says 'Only the bid operation' with no creation carve-out, while PRD/TEAM/GITHUB_PLAN require Mohammed's creation path to set it to the starting price
contradictions.sideA: ARCHITECTURE.md:511 (§9.3 field table): "Derived — never user-writable | current price | Only the bid operation (BR-07, BR-13)" — no creation-time exception. Note the adjacent row 510 DOES carve out creation for status: "System-assigned at creation | owner identity, created timestamp, initial status" — current price gets no equivalent 'initial' entry. ARCHITECTURE.md:534 (§9.4) repeats: "written only by the bid operation, in the same transaction as the bid it derives from (§13). No user, and no other code path, may write it."
contradictions.sideB: PRD.md:518 (FR-CREATE-28): "A newly created auction has a current price equal to its starting price and an empty bid history." TEAM.md:595 (M-09, Mohammed's task): "Publication behavior — auction becomes Active immediately, current price = starting price, empty history" (traces FR-CREATE-26 → 29). GITHUB_PLAN AUC-08 (Mohammed's epic) repeats it.
contradictions.whyItMatters: Mohammed's session, reading ARCHITECTURE §9.3/§9.4 literally ('no other code path may write it'), leaves current price unset at creation — then the listing (FR-LIST-02/03) and detail page (FR-DETAIL-05) have nothing to display, FR-CREATE-28 fails, and if 'unset' means NULL the step-7 comparison breaks entirely (and NULL-means-no-bids sneaks in as an implicit has-bids encoding, which FR-CREATE-28 rules out). Alternatively Mohammed implements M-09's write and a reviewer — or Rayan's session, enforcing SC-40-style 'no one but the bid operation sets current price' — flags it as a violation and 'fixes' it. Either failure costs an integration round-trip on the tightest coupling in the project.
contradictions.recommendation: Both sides are needed; the reconciliation is a carve-out mirroring what line 510 already does for status: creation initializes current price = starting price exactly once (Mohammed's path — as a column default or explicit insert value, his choice as record owner), and every write thereafter belongs exclusively to the bid operation (Rayan). Note S0-11's 'Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else' constrains only Rayan and is compatible with this. Rayan's half of the contract should state the carve-out explicitly and ask Mohammed to record it in the S0-11 agreement so neither session 'corrects' the other's write.

contradictions.topic: Status as a bid-validation input: TEAM/GITHUB_PLAN freeze status into 'the field set that bid validation depends on', while PRD LC-03 forbids deriving bid eligibility from the stored status flag — and no step of the bid operation actually consumes it
contradictions.sideA: TEAM.md:421-422 (§10.3): status is in the Required information list and "This is the field set that bid validation depends on — treat it as frozen once agreed". GITHUB_PLAN.md:263: status is one of "the six read fields" for "the auction fields Rayan's bid validation reads". TEAM.md:632 (R-03) reinforces the reading: "Server-side bid validation — authenticated, auction Active by server time, ...".
contradictions.sideB: PRD.md:1227 (LC-03): "Bidding eligibility is determined by server time against the end time, not by the stored status flag. From the end time onward, bids are rejected even if the record still says Active (BR-04, FR-BID-18, FR-END-04). This is what makes the ≤30 s processing window in FR-END-03 safe." ARCHITECTURE.md:804-844 (13.2): the only eligibility gate is step 4, "Auction exists and end time has not passed — compared against the DATABASE clock" (820-821); status appears in the step-3 re-read (817) but is consumed by NO validation step.
contradictions.whyItMatters: A session told 'bid validation depends on status' will naturally write `if status != Active then reject` as the eligibility gate. In the ≤30-second window between end time and the T1 sweep flipping the flag (or minutes/hours if the sweep fails and only T2/T3 run), the record still says Active — a status-gated implementation ACCEPTS bids after the end time. Those late bids can be the highest and thus change the winner: a fairness-breaking, outcome-corrupting bug. It fails SC-27 and BID-13's AC ("A bid at or after the end time is always rejected — even if the record still says Active", GITHUB_PLAN.md:456) and silently defeats the design decision that makes the scheduled-sweep architecture safe (ARCHITECTURE.md:1006-1014).
contradictions.recommendation: LC-03 wins unconditionally — it is the PRD's explicit lifecycle rule and the architecture's stated safety premise. Status stays in the record and in the read set (Rayan writes it at close; it is the finalization idempotency marker per ARCHITECTURE.md:1029 step 2, the sweep's not-yet-finalized predicate, and a display value), but Rayan's half of S0-11 should annotate it: 'status is read for presentation and the ended short-circuit only; bid eligibility is decided solely by end time vs the database clock; a bid gate on status is a bug (LC-03)'. This one line prevents the most natural misreading of the frozen list.

contradictions.topic: Realtime payload content: PRD requires bidder display names (and forbids surplus internal identifiers) in payloads, but the ARCHITECTURE mechanism broadcasts committed row changes from rows that store only internal identity — and its 'satisfied structurally' privacy claim covers only emails
contradictions.sideA: PRD.md:1304 (RT-S1): "Real-time updates must contain only data the recipient is already entitled to see: amount, bidder display name, timestamp, price, status, outcome." PRD.md:1305 (RT-S2): "Email addresses, internal account identifiers beyond what public display requires, and any other private data must never appear in a real-time payload." PRD.md:645 (FR-BID-22a): public history shows "display names only — never email addresses, never internal identifiers". TEAM.md:443 (§10.5): consumers of the outcome need "Winner identifier and display name".
contradictions.sideB: ARCHITECTURE.md:928-939 (§14.1): the broadcast is "Supabase Realtime detects the committed change... Realtime carries only what was already committed. It is a projection of database state" — and the committed rows contain no display name: the bid record stores "auction, bidder identity, amount, timestamp" (ARCHITECTURE.md:518) and the auction record stores "winner identity" (ARCHITECTURE.md:512). ARCHITECTURE.md:962-966 (§14.4) then claims RT-S1 AND RT-S2 are "satisfied structurally, not by filtering" — but the structural argument given ('emails live in the auth record') only proves no EMAIL can leak; it says nothing about display names being present or internal identifiers being absent.
contradictions.whyItMatters: Rayan owns realtime delivery and 'decides what is broadcast' (TEAM.md §10.4). Built as ARCHITECTURE describes — a raw row-change projection — the live payload (a) cannot show the new bidder's display name in the history list within the 2-second budget (NFR-RT-01, FR-BID-23) without a client-side join no document defines, and (b) carries raw bidder/owner/winner identifiers, which a reviewer reading RT-S2/FR-BID-22a can reasonably call a violation. The tempting fix — denormalizing display name onto the bid row or the auction record at close — breaks FR-PROF-05 (PRD.md:466: display-name edits must not retroactively alter history attribution... a stored name string freezes it wrongly OR a live join changes it, one of the two must be chosen deliberately), breaks 'nothing is stored in two places' (ARCHITECTURE.md:493), and per BR-39/A-T4 the internal identifier must remain the attribution source of truth. Three sessions will pick three different resolutions, and this payload rides the exact auction-record change S0-11 governs.
contradictions.recommendation: This cannot be resolved by either developer alone — it must be an explicit line in the S0-11/realtime agreement.
