The doc-consistent resolution: rows keep identifiers only (BR-39, FR-PROF-05); clients resolve identifier → display name from the public profile table (display name is the sole public profile field, SEC-P2, so this leaks nothing); and RT-S2's phrase 'beyond what public display requires' is read as PERMITTING the opaque identifiers in payloads precisely because public display requires them for name resolution — while FR-BID-22a's 'never internal identifiers' is scoped to what is RENDERED, not what is transported. Record that interpretation (or an agreed curated-broadcast alternative) in writing; also flag that ARCHITECTURE §14.4's 'structurally satisfied' claim overstates what it proves.

contradictions.topic: TEAM.md's own write-permission sentence omits Rayan's per-bid current-price write, contradicting the feedback path three lines below and the S0-11 AC
contradictions.sideA: TEAM.md:373 (§9.3 Avoiding duplication): Rayan "never writes to the auction record except for the fields explicitly assigned to him at close (status, final price, winner, close time)" — read literally, this forbids the bid operation's current-price update.
contradictions.sideB: TEAM.md:376-378 (§9.3 The feedback path, same section): "Rayan writes back to the auction in exactly two situations... 1. On each accepted bid — the auction's current price becomes the new bid amount. 2. At close...". GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 (S0-11 AC): "Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else". ARCHITECTURE.md:674 (§11.2): "Bid operation → ✅ current price only".
contradictions.whyItMatters: A session skimming §9.3's table (and this table is where the six-field list also lives, so it WILL be quoted) could design Mohammed's access path or the RLS/privilege layout with no current-price write grant for the bid operation — at which point steps 8+9 of the bid transaction cannot commit and every bid fails, or the grant gets added ad hoc without being part of the agreed contract. Risk is contained because the correction is three lines below in the same section, but this is the third place in TEAM.md §9.3/§10.3 where 'current price' has been dropped from the contract text (with lines 372 and 421), which is a pattern, not a typo.
contradictions.recommendation: The feedback path (TEAM.md:376-381) and GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 win — they agree with ARCHITECTURE's access model. Rayan's half of S0-11 should quote the two-situation write rule verbatim as the definitive statement of his writes (per-bid: current price only; at close: status, final price, winner, close time only; nothing else ever), and note that TEAM.md:373's sentence is incomplete and should be amended to '...except current price on each accepted bid and the four fields assigned at close'.

contradictions.topic: S0-11's authoritative citation points to the wrong document: 'ARCHITECTURE §10.3' is Password reset, not the auction record contract
contradictions.sideA: GITHUB_PLAN.md:263 (S0-11) cites "ARCHITECTURE §10.3" twice as the source for the auction-record contract: "TEAM.md task M-01, ARCHITECTURE §10.3 — agree the auction fields..." and "Rayan writes current price on each accepted bid and nothing else (ARCHITECTURE §10.3)".

A session resolving 'ARCHITECTURE §10.3' lands on password reset, concludes the pointer is stale, and either (a) treats the 'nothing else' write-exclusivity clause as unsupported and negotiable, or (b) goes hunting and finds TEAM.md §10.3 — whose six-field list is the WRONG one (contradiction 2), lending the wrong list the authority of 'the cited source'. contradictions.topic: Who supplies the listing's current price: TEAM.md makes M-10 depend on 'Current price from Rayan' derived from bid history, while ARCHITECTURE §9.4 resolves that Mohammed's pages read the field directly with no aggregation
contradictions.sideA: TEAM.md:267 (§8 ownership changes): "The listing shows each auction's current price... That value is derived from bid history, which is Rayan's. Mohammed builds the listing; Rayan supplies how the price is obtained." TEAM.md:596 (M-10's dependency column): "Current price from Rayan".
contradictions.sideB: ARCHITECTURE.md:531-538 (§9.4, explicitly marked 'The current-price question — resolved'): "The current price lives on the auction record — one read, no aggregation, fast listing and detail pages (NFR-PERF-01/02)... Mohammed's pages read the field. Rayan's operation writes it. Neither computes it independently. This resolves the ownership ambiguity without splitting the data."
contradictions.whyItMatters: Mohammed's session, reading TEAM.md, may block M-10 waiting for a price-obtaining mechanism from Rayan that ARCHITECTURE says should not exist, or Rayan's session may build an aggregate-from-history helper for the listing — duplicating the fact ('Nothing is stored in two places', ARCHITECTURE.md:493) and risking a listing price that disagrees with the record during the very race windows BR-13 exists to eliminate. Mostly a wasted-coordination cost, but it sits on the same current-price seam as the critical contradictions.
contradictions.recommendation: ARCHITECTURE §9.4 wins — it is the later document and explicitly announces itself as the resolution of TEAM.md §6's open question. 'Rayan supplies how the price is obtained' should be read as: Rayan's bid operation maintains the field's correctness (BR-13), and Mohammed reads the auction record's current-price column directly in the listing query. Rayan's half of S0-11 should state that he provides NO query helper for the listing and that M-10's dependency is satisfied by the field itself — plus the has-bids label state from contradiction 1, which is the one thing the listing genuinely cannot get from the price column.

approach: A stored discriminator on the auction record: add `bid_count integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` to Mohammed's auctions table, incremented by Rayan's bid operation in the same transaction as the bid insert and the current-price update (ARCHITECTURE.md:836-838 steps 8-9 become a three-part inseparable write). The BR-28 branch (PRD.md:767) is then decided by a single column read on the very row the operation already locks. The approach's textual anchor is ARCHITECTURE.md:817 (13.2 step 3), the only occurrence of "bid count" in all four documents: "Re-read auction state INSIDE the lock — owner, status, end time, current price, bid count" — which reads most naturally as a row attribute of the auction, since it is listed as auction state and everything else on that line is one. Its strongest practical argument is not the bid function (where a derived EXISTS works equally well) but the read side: AUC-14 (GITHUB_PLAN.md:382) and FR-DETAIL-06/FR-LIST-03 (PRD.md:545, PRD.md:525) require every price display to distinguish "Starting price: 100 SAR (no bids yet)" from "Current bid: 250 SAR", ARCHITECTURE.md:538 forbids Mohammed computing anything, and NFR-PERF-01/02 push for one-read listing rows — a column beside current_price gives Mohammed the label with zero joins and zero aggregation, exactly the pattern §9.4 (ARCHITECTURE.md:531-538) already blessed for current price. Bonus: because the per-bid UPDATE now changes price and counter in one committed row change, the AUC-14 label flip rides the same auction-record realtime broadcast as the price (ARCHITECTURE.md:928-939, 953) with no extra channel. `bid_count` is chosen over a `has_bids` boolean because bids are append-only with no delete path (BR-05, SC-15 PRD.md:1628, BID-01 GITHUB_PLAN.md:444), so the counter is monotonically non-decreasing (no decrement bugs possible in the sanctioned architecture), it matches the §13.2 diagram's own words, and it gives NFR-REL-04's "accepted count equals history count" check (BID-03, GITHUB_PLAN.md:446) a stored operand plus a "5 bids" display affordance. The count remains independently recomputable from history at any time, mirroring the §9.4 verification invariant for current price (ARCHITECTURE.md:536).
discriminator: `bid_count = 0` means no bids yet (inclusive branch, amount >= starting_price per BR-29); `bid_count > 0` means has bids (strict branch, amount > current_price per BR-03). The value is read in the same `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` that acquires the row lock (ARCHITECTURE.md:811-817 steps 2-3), so it is never stale, and it is incremented inside the same transaction as the bid insert and price update, so it can never disagree with committed history — by the identical one-transaction argument ARCHITECTURE.md:535 uses for current price ("Because both writes happen in one transaction, they cannot diverge"). Critically, the discriminator is NEVER price equality: current_price == starting_price is true both before any bid (M-09, TEAM.md:595) and immediately after SC-55's first equal bid, so price comparison fails SC-56; bid_count distinguishes those two states unambiguously.

Bidder B was queued on the row lock the whole time (ARCHITECTURE.md:812-814); under READ COMMITTED, when the lock releases, B's SELECT FOR UPDATE re-evaluates against the newly committed row version and reads bid_count = 1, current_price = 100.00. B therefore takes the STRICT branch: 100.00 > 100.00 → FALSE → rejected with the distinct race message "Someone bid before you — the current price is now 100 SAR" (ARCHITECTURE.md:903, SC-18). Exactly one acceptance at the 100.00 price level — BR-11/BR-12 hold, matching the V-1 verification target (GITHUB_PLAN.md:299). -- Steps 2-3 (ARCHITECTURE.md:812-818): lock and re-read; anything read before this is stale
SELECT owner_id, status, end_time, starting_price, current_price
  INTO v
  FROM auction
 WHERE id = p_auction_id
   FOR UPDATE;
IF NOT FOUND THEN RETURN reject('auction_not_found'); END IF;            -- the 'existence' guarantee
IF now() >= v.end_time THEN RETURN reject('auction_ended'); END IF;      -- BR-04/LC-03: DB clock, NEVER v.status

-- BR-21 well-formedness: p_amount > 0 AND scale(p_amount) <= 2; NO maximum check

IF (v.current_price IS NULL     AND p_amount >= v.starting_price)   -- no bids yet  → inclusive (BR-29, SC-55)
OR (v.current_price IS NOT NULL AND p_amount >  v.current_price)    -- has bids     → strict    (BR-03, SC-56)
THEN
  INSERT INTO bid (auction_id, bidder_id, amount, placed_at)
       VALUES (p_auction_id, v_bidder, p_amount, now());                 -- step 8 (BR-18)
  UPDATE auction SET current_price = p_amount WHERE id = p_auction_id;   -- step 9 (BR-13) — flips the
                                                                         -- discriminator NULL→NOT NULL
                                                                         -- atomically with the bid
ELSIF v.current_price IS NULL THEN RETURN reject('below_starting_price', v.starting_price);
ELSE                               RETURN reject('not_above_current',    v.current_price);
END IF;

Inside the lock: current_price IS NOT NULL → strict branch → 100.00 > 100.00 is FALSE → REJECTED with "Your bid must be higher than 100 SAR" (ARCHITECTURE.md:903); nothing written, state unchanged (BR-23). The equality allowance cannot leak to a second bid because eligibility was never inferred from price comparison — the state is structurally NOT NULL regardless of the values being equal. C then bids 100.01: NOT NULL branch, 100.01 > 100.00 TRUE → ACCEPTED (BR-32: no increment floor — 0.01 is a valid raise); bid appended, current_price := 100.01. Matches SC-56 (PRD.md:1624), EC-23 (PRD.md:1414), and walkthrough steps 5-6 (PRD.md:1740).
concurrencySafety: Yes — and this is the approach's strongest property: the discriminator is a column OF THE LOCKED ROW, so there is no cross-table visibility question at all. Two simultaneous first bids of 100 SAR on the same auction: both transactions reach SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the same auction row; B acquires the lock, reads current_price IS NULL, accepts 100, sets current_price = 100.00, commits; the lock releases. C, which was queued on that row lock, then proceeds — and under READ COMMITTED (Supabase/PostgreSQL default), FOR UPDATE re-fetches the LATEST COMMITTED row version after the lock wait (PostgreSQL's EvalPlanQual recheck), so C's re-read sees current_price = 100.00 NOT NULL → strict branch → 100.00 > 100.00 false → rejected with the distinct concurrency message "Someone bid before you — the current price is now 100 SAR" (ARCHITECTURE.md:858, 904; EC-01). Exactly one acceptance per price level (BR-12), one definitive ordering (BR-11), resolving precisely as ARCHITECTURE.md:858 describes. The write that flips the discriminator (step 9's UPDATE) is on the same row the lock guards and in the same transaction as the bid insert (steps 8-9 inseparable), so no interleaving can observe NULL alongside an existing bid or NOT NULL with an empty history. Contrast with the EXISTS-on-bids alternative: that is also safe under the row lock, but its correctness depends on a second table's snapshot visibility after a lock wait — a subtlety a vibe-coder session can silently get wrong; nullness cannot be read stale because the lock and the fact live on the same tuple. Two caveats for V-1 (GITHUB_PLAN.md:299) to confirm: (1) this analysis assumes READ COMMITTED — under REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE the queued transaction gets a serialization error instead of a clean re-read (still never a wrong acceptance, but the error must be mapped to the concurrency rejection message); (2) the function must contain no code path that reads the auction row before the FOR UPDATE and reuses those values (ARCHITECTURE.md:818: 'Anything read before the lock is already stale').
weaknesses: IT AMENDS THE PRD, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE COST. FR-CREATE-28 (PRD.md:518), BR-13 (PRD.md:752), BR-07's rationale (PRD.md:741), ARCHITECTURE §9.4's zero-tolerance invariant (ARCHITECTURE.md:534, restated in BID-05's AC at GITHUB_PLAN.md:448), ARCHITECTURE.md:741's diagram, and TEAM.md:595 M-09 all state 'current price = starting price before any bid' in plain language. The competing design (derive has-bids via EXISTS on the bids table inside the lock) satisfies every one of those sentences UNCHANGED and needs no PRD edit. S0-11 exists to agree a contract, not to reopen a Decided product invariant; TEAM.md:374 explicitly forbids renegotiating the record mid-sprint, and this approach's very first act is a ~10-site PR across all four documents requiring three-developer plus product sign-off. If Mohammed pushes back on nothing else, he will push back on this — correctly.

NULL PROPAGATES TO EVERY CONSUMER FOREVER. Every read of current_price in three codebases must handle NULL: detail price region (AUC-14), every listing row (FR-LIST-02/03), minimum-bid display and its client-side realtime recompute (ARCHITECTURE.md:953), seller view, outcome views. Three vibe-coder Claude sessions independently handling nullable money is a wide surface for 'null SAR', NaN, or a crash at 375 px — and NFR-DAT-08 (PRD.md:1547, one consistent format everywhere) multiplies every such miss into a visible inconsistency. The non-null designs confine the no-bids special case to ONE code site (the bid function); this design exports it to every display site in the product.

ONE COALESCE IN THE WRONG PLACE SILENTLY DESTROYS THE CONTRACT. FR-LIST-03's display wording ('current price must be the starting price when there are no bids') actively invites Mohammed's access path to return COALESCE(current_price, starting_price) — and Rayan reads ONLY through that path (TEAM.md:373/422). If the coalesce happens in the shared path rather than at the rendering edge, the discriminator vanishes, the bid function's IS NULL branch becomes unreachable, SC-55 fails, and the price-equality ambiguity this design was built to kill reappears one layer up — with no error anywhere. The contract must carry an explicit negative clause ('the access path returns the raw nullable column; fallback only at render'), and negative clauses are exactly what separate Claude sessions are worst at honoring.

SORT/FILTER AND AGGREGATES NEED COALESCE EVERYWHERE, FOREVER. Price sorting/filtering is Should Have S6/FR-LIST-12 (PRD.md:376, 536): when it arrives, ORDER BY current_price mis-clusters all no-bid auctions (NULLS LAST on ASC, NULLS FIRST on DESC), and a price-range WHERE current_price BETWEEN ... silently DROPS every no-bid auction from results. Every future query must remember COALESCE(current_price, starting_price) — a latent, invisible bug class planted now and detonating after MVP, when nobody re-reads S0-11.

NULL-AS-FLAG IS SEMANTIC OVERLOADING OF A KNOWN SQL TRAP. Encoding 'has bids' in the absence of a value means the naive comparison p_amount > current_price evaluates to NULL (falsy) on a fresh auction: a session that forgets the IS NULL branch rejects ALL first bids. It fails safe (rejects rather than wrongly accepts, so SC-55 catches it), but TEAM.md:632's own abbreviation of R-03 ('strictly greater than current price') shows exactly this forgetting already happening in the team's documents. The design's correctness depends on every future edit of the bid function preserving a three-valued-logic branch.

IT WEAKENS BR-13'S SINGLE-DEFINITION PURPOSE. BR-13 exists to give listing, detail, and validation ONE notion of 'the price' (PRD.md:752, rationale column). Under this design 'the price' is a nullable column for validation and a two-field fallback expression for display — two notions where the PRD demanded one. The rewritten BR-13 must define both and say which contexts use which, or the ambiguity BR-13 was created to remove returns in new clothes.

THE current_price >= starting_price CHECK SMEARS THE OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY. It encodes a fragment of Rayan's BR-28 rule inside Mohammed's DDL — useful defense-in-depth, but now a piece of bid validation lives in a file Mohammed owns (TEAM.md §11 shared-file rules), and a future change to Rayan's rule requires a migration in Mohammed's territory. Dropping the CHECK keeps the boundary clean at the cost of the safety net; the contract must pick one explicitly.

THE DOC-CONSISTENT ALTERNATIVE IS SIMPLY CHEAPER. An EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bid WHERE auction_id = ...) inside the same row lock delivers the identical SC-55/SC-56 behavior, keeps all six fields non-null, requires ZERO document changes beyond writing the derivation rule into S0-11, and confines all special-casing to the one function Rayan owns. Its only real costs are one extra indexed probe per bid and a subtler concurrency-visibility argument. Honest bottom line: nullable current_price wins on structural elegance (discriminator on the locked row, creation write eliminated, display distinction free) and loses on total cost of adoption — and if Mohammed declines to reopen FR-CREATE-28/BR-13, the EXISTS derivation is the fallback Rayan's half should name in the same breath.
